Build landing, product and collection pages with AI. Find what costs you sales. A/B test the fix.

PageFly is an AI CRO funnel builder and AI page builder for Shopify. Build your home page, product page, collection page, landing page and custom page with AI, a drag and drop page editor or templates. Then improve each funnel step: AI Page Checkup finds what costs you sales, FlyMate fixes sections by prompt, and A/B tests, heatmaps and funnel analytics show what works. The PageFly MCP connector works in Claude, ChatGPT and Sidekick. Localize per Shopify Market. Cart drawer with upsells (beta).

Feedback submitted

Merchants say this app makes it easy to build and customize Shopify pages without coding, using templates, modular elements, and AI tools. They highlight strong design flexibility, mobile/desktop optimization, and better conversions and sales from improved landing and product pages. Performance is described as smooth, and many praise the 24/7 live chat support as exceptionally fast, patient, and effective, especially for non‑technical merchants.

November 7, 2026

Updated Review — Excellent Legacy Editor, Disappointing Gen 2 Experience

I originally left PageFly a very positive review after using its legacy editor to build and customize our Wallhogs website nearly 9 years ago. At the time, I found it intuitive, flexible, and well-designed, with clearly labeled controls that made creating custom layouts relatively straightforward.

Unfortunately, my experience with PageFly Gen 2 while building another Shopify website has been considerably different.

As an experienced website designer with a background in the e-commerce industry, I find the new Flex Block-based editor unnecessarily restrictive and cumbersome compared with the legacy version.

Many of the tools and controls that made the original editor so effective have either been removed, reorganized, or replaced with less intuitive alternatives. The right-hand settings panel is particularly frustrating. Controls have been renamed or grouped in ways that make their functions difficult to understand, and there is little contextual guidance explaining what they actually do.

The learning curve has increased substantially, even for someone already familiar with PageFly.

Responsive design has also become unnecessarily complicated. Tasks such as aligning images of different proportions within a three-column layout now require manual adjustments across multiple device breakpoints.

Even more concerning, I've encountered instances where layouts display correctly in the Gen 2 editor but render differently on the published Shopify storefront.

The legacy editor allowed me to concentrate on designing the website. Gen 2 frequently forces me to concentrate on figuring out how to operate the editor.

I still believe PageFly's original product was excellent, which makes this redesign particularly disappointing.

I hope the development team seriously considers restoring the flexibility, intuitive controls, clear labeling, and designer-focused functionality that made the legacy editor so effective.

At this point, I would be reluctant to use Gen 2 for another custom website project.

Hi memesbyapril,

Thank you sincerely for taking the time to share such detailed and thoughtful feedback. We truly value the perspective of someone who has experienced both our legacy editor and Gen 2, and we understand why the changes around Flex Block, the reorganized settings panel, responsive editing, and differences between the editor and published storefront have been frustrating for you.

We especially appreciate how clearly you explained what worked well in the legacy editor and what now feels less intuitive in Gen 2. Feedback like yours gives our team a much better understanding of where the experience needs to improve. Our team is continuing to release updates and improvements to Gen 2 on a regular basis, and we’ll make sure your specific feedback is shared with the relevant team and considered as part of that ongoing work.
